description: Postgres health — connections, cache hit ratio, transaction rate, and database size. Populated by postgres-exporter. First place to look when API latency spikes: is the DB hot?

panels.description:
**What:** current active connections per database vs the configured `max_connections` ceiling.

**Why:** Postgres rejects new connections once max is reached — APIs hang or 500. The ratio is early-warning before that point.

**Watch for:** > 80% sustained triggers `PostgresConnectionsHigh`. Options to relieve: lower `DATABASE_POOL_SIZE` on the API side, scale Postgres up, or hunt for connection leaks (long-lived connections without active queries are usually a forgotten cleanup).
panels.title: Active connections (per database) vs max_connections

panels.description:
**What:** buffer-cache hit ratio across all databases, computed as `blks_hit / (blks_hit + blks_read)`.

**Why:** Postgres reads pages from disk or from `shared_buffers`. Disk reads are 100–1000× slower. The hit ratio tells you whether queries are finding hot data in memory.

**Watch for:** sustained < 95% = hot data doesn't fit in `shared_buffers`. Either bump that setting (single biggest Postgres tuning lever), or a query is scanning much more than it should (likely missing an index, found via `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`).
panels.title: Cache hit ratio (target: >95%)

panels.description:
**What:** stacked commits + rollbacks per second across all databases.

**Why:** baseline DB workload metric. Lets you correlate API traffic with DB pressure.

**Watch for:** rollback ratio creeping up = user errors or a buggy code path. Sudden TX-rate drop without a matching API-rate drop = something blocking writes (lock contention, replication issue, full disk).
panels.title: Transactions per second (commits + rollbacks)

panels.description:
**What:** on-disk size per database over time.

**Why:** capacity-planning signal. Predicts when you'll need a larger volume.

**Watch for:** sudden step-changes = a new table or unbounded log/audit insertion. Steady linear growth = normal; project the line to know when you'll hit disk pressure (`DiskSpaceLow` triggers at 10% free).
panels.title: Database size

panels.description:
**What:** wall-clock duration of the single longest-running active transaction.

**Why:** long transactions block VACUUM and accumulate dead tuples. The classic 'why is Postgres slow and only restarting fixes it' cause.

**Watch for:** > 60s (orange) = a query that should be async or chunked is running synchronously. > 5min (red) = real problem — often a forgotten `BEGIN` in an interactive session, a stuck migration, or a backup job holding a snapshot.
panels.title: Longest running transaction

panels.description:
**What:** count of deadlocks Postgres detected and broke per minute.

**Why:** Postgres resolves deadlocks automatically (it kills the younger transaction) but each one is a failed user request.

**Watch for:** any sustained non-zero rate = your code has a lock-order bug. Classic cause: two transactions acquire `accounts` then `memberships` in one code path but reverse order in another. Trace the offending SQL via the API logs dashboard's database-queries panel.
panels.title: Deadlocks per minute
